links.outcome: Biomarker distribution differences between development and external cohorts indicating dataset shift
links.effect: Biomarker distribution differences across ADNI and A4 were consistent with dataset shift, and cross-cohort transfer degraded predictive values despite preserved discrimination.
links.quote: Biomarker distribution differences across cohorts were consistent with dataset shift.

links.outcome: Performance of externally trained models on another cohort without retraining (AUC, NPV)
links.effect: Cross-cohort AUC attenuated ~4-7%; NPV fell from 0.831 to 0.644 under ADNI→A4 transfer (~19 percentage points); calibration systematically misestimated probabilities.
links.quote: NPV declined from 0.831 to 0.644 under ADNI→A4 transfer (∼19 percentage points) despite preserved discrimination.

links.outcome: Predictive values and net benefit under cross-cohort transfer with differing prevalence
links.effect: NPV dropped ~19 points under transfer; decision curve analysis showed reduced net clinical benefit; prevalence differences critically affect NPV.
links.quote: Calibration instability and prevalence differences critically affect NPV, highlighting the need for cross-cohort validation, calibration assessment, and assay harmonization before clinical implementation.

links.outcome: Calibration of transferred models without local retraining
links.effect: Calibration analyses demonstrated systematic probability misestimation when models were transferred without retraining.
links.quote: Calibration analyses demonstrated systematic probability misestimation, and decision curve analysis showed reduced net clinical benefit.

unlisted_practices: assay harmonization across platforms before clinical implementation

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating cross-cohort generalizability and calibration-driven degradation of plasma biomarker machine learning models across independent cohorts (ADNI and A4). It does not test an organizational safeguard or deployment intervention directly.
